commands.review_summary:
The PR makes Railway `Stop` reject unclaimed service IDs before provider API setup, updates the Railway regression test and docs/provider metadata, and adds a changelog entry.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: current main routes a caller-supplied Railway service ID through `LatestDeployment` and `StopDeployment` without a claim, and the existing fake API test verifies that behavior. I did not run a live Railway stop because it would require real provider credentials and a real service.

target.title: fix(railway): reject unowned service stops
target.body:
## Summary

- make Railway `stop` fail closed before authentication, inventory lookup, or mutation because out-of-band services have no verifiable Crabbox ownership claim
- preserve Railway `status` and `list` as read-only inspection paths; direct operators to Railway for destructive lifecycle actions
- replace the prior mutation test with a regression test proving an unclaimed service ID causes zero Railway API calls
- update the Railway guide, generated provider matrix, metadata, and changelog to match the supported boundary

This follows the lifecycle policy in `VISION.md`: destructive operations require exact provider/resource/claim ownership, while legacy or external adoption must be explicit and conflict-safe. Railway currently has no adoption contract, so a raw service ID cannot authorize a stop.

Closes https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/833

## Verification

Exact candidate: `c718a781f01b85d6fdd921cb2c140958e798a06a`

- `go test -race ./internal/providers/railway`
- `go vet ./internal/providers/railway`
- `go test -race ./...`
- `scripts/check-docs.sh`
- `node scripts/generate-provider-matrix.mjs`
- `git diff --check`
- autoreview clean, confidence 0.86

## Live proof

Built the real CLI with `go build -trimpath -o bin/crabbox ./cmd/crabbox`, started a listening local GraphQL spy, then invoked `crabbox stop --provider railway --id svc-unclaimed` with complete project/environment/API configuration and a test-only token. The CLI returned the ownership rejection and the spy recorded exactly zero HTTP requests. This proves the changed end-to-end behavior without risking a real Railway service.

## Compatibility

This intentionally removes Crabbox's unsafe raw-ID Railway stop behavior. Existing services remain inspectable through `status` and `list`; stop them through Railway until Crabbox has an explicit adoption and exact-claim contract.
